title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.
intro: This training programme equips directors and senior managers of regulated firms within cross-border groups to govern the group and its local entities well: structuring the business, balancing group direction with local accountability and dealing with multiple supervisors.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give boards and senior managers of firms that operate across borders a practical understanding of how group structures, intragroup arrangements and cross-border access shape governance, risk and regulatory exposure. Participants leave able to balance group direction with the independence of local boards, oversee intragroup services and booking models, manage conflicts between group and entity, and engage confidently with home and host supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: Group structures and why they matter to supervisors, subsidiaries versus branches, local board independence and group direction, intragroup outsourcing and service agreements, booking models and substance, passporting and third-country access, dealing with multiple supervisors and colleges, conflicts between group and local entity, and group stress and recovery.
Intended Audience: Chairs, executive, non-executive and independent directors of regulated subsidiaries, and of parent and holding companies
Country heads, branch managers and senior managers responsible for a local entity within a wider group
Group and local heads of compliance, risk, legal, governance and regulatory affairs
Learning Objectives: Explain how group structures, legal entities and branches determine regulatory responsibility and supervisory scrutiny
Evaluate the balance between group direction and the independence and accountability of local boards
Oversee intragroup outsourcing, service agreements and booking models so that local substance and control are demonstrable
Assess cross-border access options, including passporting, branches and third-country routes, and their governance consequences
Manage relationships with home and host supervisors and prepare for college and joint engagement
Identify and resolve conflicts between group and local entity interests, including in stress, and agree an action plan
sections.Structure and Format: Nine modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions for a group or subsidiary board. Each module combines a short briefing with case studies, scenarios and a director question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's group structure and markets.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board, senior management or control function experience in a firm that is part of a group or operates across borders is helpful. No legal background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Supervisory Colleges (2014)

modules.title: Group Structures and Why They Matter
modules.summary: How regulated firms organise across borders through holding companies, subsidiaries and branches, and why supervisors look at the group as well as the licensed entity.
objectives: Explain common cross-border group structures in investment, funds, payments and crypto-asset businesses
Identify where regulated and unregulated entities create gaps or risks
Explain how consolidated and group-wide supervision affects the local firm
syllabus: Holding companies, operating subsidiaries, branches and service companies
Why groups grow complex: tax, licences, acquisitions and legacy
Consolidated and group-wide supervision from the firm's side
Mapping the group: legal entities, licences, people and money flows

modules.title: Subsidiary or Branch: Structuring for Access and Control
modules.summary: The governance, capital, regulatory and operational trade-offs between serving a market through a subsidiary, a branch or cross-border services, and how the choice shapes supervisory expectations.
objectives: Compare subsidiaries, branches and cross-border services as routes to market
Assess the governance and resourcing consequences of each structure
Anticipate when a host authority may require a subsidiary or added safeguards
syllabus: Branch versus subsidiary: capital, governance, liability and resolvability
Cross-border services without a local presence
Host expectations of systemically or retail-significant branches
Case study: restructuring a branch network into a regulated subsidiary

modules.title: Local Board Independence and Group Direction
modules.summary: How the board of a regulated subsidiary discharges its own duties while operating within group strategy, policies and reporting lines, and what supervisors mean by a local board that is not a rubber stamp.
objectives: Explain the duties of subsidiary directors to the entity, its customers and its regulators
Evaluate the balance between group policies, matrix reporting and local decision-making
Apply practical tests of whether the local board genuinely governs
syllabus: Directors' duties in a subsidiary: whose interests come first
Group policies, local adoption and documented deviations
Matrix management, dual-hatted executives and independent directors
Board question set: is our board governing or ratifying

modules.title: Intragroup Outsourcing and Service Agreements
modules.summary: How local entities rely on group functions, technology and staff, and how to document, oversee and evidence those arrangements to the same standard as an external outsourcing.
objectives: Identify intragroup dependencies on people, systems, data and functions
Assess intragroup service agreements, service levels and exit arrangements
Oversee group-provided services so that responsibility is demonstrably retained locally
syllabus: Why intragroup does not mean low risk: the supervisor's view
Service agreements: scope, standards, data, audit rights and termination
Oversight, management information and escalation for group services
Operational resilience and continuity when the group provider fails

modules.title: Booking Models, Substance and Local Control
modules.summary: How groups decide where business is originated, executed, booked and risk-managed, and how to demonstrate that the licensed entity has real substance and control over the risks on its books.
objectives: Explain common booking and remote-booking models and the risks they create
Assess whether the local entity has adequate people, decision-making and risk management on the ground
Prepare the evidence of substance that host supervisors expect
syllabus: Origination, execution, booking and risk management across entities
Back-to-back and remote booking: transfer of risk and its limits
Substance tests: senior people, decision-making, controls and records
Red flags supervisors look for in empty or letterbox entities

modules.title: Passporting and Third-Country Access
modules.summary: How regional passporting, reliance and third-country regimes allow firms to serve clients across borders, the conditions and limits attached to them, and the governance needed to stay within them.
objectives: Explain the main models of cross-border market access in generic terms
Assess the regulatory perimeter risks of serving clients from outside their jurisdiction
Design governance and controls that keep cross-border activity within its permissions
syllabus: Passporting, equivalence, reliance and third-country regimes
Reverse solicitation, delegation and other routes and their limits
Losing access: planning for a change in regime or recognition
Controls over cross-border marketing, onboarding and servicing

modules.title: Dealing with Multiple Supervisors
modules.summary: How home and host supervisors divide responsibilities, share information and coordinate through colleges, and how the group and its local entities manage engagement, consistency and conflicting demands.
objectives: Explain home and host responsibilities and how supervisors share information
Coordinate consistent, candid engagement across the group's supervisors
Handle conflicting supervisory demands and joint reviews or college engagement
syllabus: Home and host roles, information-sharing and memoranda of understanding
Supervisory colleges and joint risk assessment from the firm's side
One message, many regulators: coordinating notifications and responses
Exercise: responding to conflicting requests from two supervisors

modules.title: Conflicts Between the Group and the Local Entity
modules.summary: Where the interests of the group and a regulated subsidiary diverge, from capital and liquidity transfers to pricing, client allocation and strategy, and how directors identify, manage and record those conflicts.
objectives: Identify common conflicts between group and local entity interests
Apply a structured approach to managing and recording group conflicts
Challenge group decisions that disadvantage the entity, its customers or its regulators
syllabus: Intragroup funding, dividends, guarantees and transfer pricing
Client allocation, product shelf and revenue sharing across entities
Local directors' conflicts when they also hold group roles
Case study: a group restructuring the local board does not support

modules.title: Group Stress, Recovery and Wind-Down: Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a cross-border stress scenario, covering contagion, recovery and wind-down planning, ring-fencing pressures and communication with supervisors, followed by an action plan.
objectives: Identify how stress spreads between entities and jurisdictions in a group
Assess the local entity's recovery and wind-down arrangements in a group context
Produce an action plan for strengthening group and local governance
syllabus: Contagion channels: funding, services, reputation and shared clients
Recovery and wind-down planning for a group entity
Simulation: a parent in difficulty and two supervisors seeking reassurance
Workshop: the group and local governance action plan

related.title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.

related.title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.

related.title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.

related.title: Induction for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: A ten-module induction giving new directors of regulated firms the grounding to discharge their duties, understand supervisory expectations and oversee the firm's risks.
